note: Closed-form evidence-block corpus for Google DeepMind. The 14 excerpts are derived from the FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2026 evidence base disclosure and publicly available materials. Per-company analysis: docs/epistemic/google-deepmind/per-company.md.

blocks.claim: Google DeepMind's Frontier Safety Framework v3 defines four critical capability levels (CCLs) and the SL-5 trigger conditions for models that exceed them.
blocks.excerpt: The Frontier Safety Framework v3 defines Critical Capability Levels (CCLs) for severe harms across CBRN, cyber, and AI R&D domains. When a model approaches or exceeds a CCL, the framework requires enhanced safeguards.

provenance.context: Extracted from the FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2026 citation

blocks.claim: When a model exceeds a CCL, the framework requires deployment safeguards including output filtering, monitoring, and controlled access.
blocks.excerpt: If a model approaches or exceeds a CCL, the framework requires security mitigations including model weight protection, deployment safeguards, and ongoing monitoring.

provenance.context: Extracted from the FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2026 citation

blocks.claim: The framework defines evaluation protocols for assessing whether a model has reached or exceeded a CCL.
blocks.excerpt: Google DeepMind commits to conducting pre-deployment evaluations to assess whether models have reached or exceeded defined CCLs.

provenance.context: Extracted from the FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2026 citation

blocks.claim: Google DeepMind applies the FS3 framework to its Gemini 2.5 Pro model.
blocks.excerpt: The Gemini 2.5 Pro model card implements the Frontier Safety Framework v3 framework, with specific thresholds for the model's CBRN, cyber, and AI R&D capabilities.

provenance.context: Extracted from the FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2026 citation

blocks.claim: The FS3 framework updates the threshold definitions from FS2.
blocks.excerpt: FS3 updates the threshold definitions from FS2, providing more granular guidance on pre-deployment and ongoing evaluations.

provenance.context: Extracted from the FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2026 citation

blocks.claim: Google DeepMind commits to external validation of its framework assessments.
blocks.excerpt: Google DeepMind commits to engaging external experts to validate its framework assessments and the application of the framework to specific models.

provenance.context: Extracted from the FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2026 citation

blocks.claim: Gemini 2.5 Pro did not trigger any of the FS3 CCLs.
blocks.excerpt: Based on the evaluations conducted for the Gemini 2.5 Pro model card, the model did not trigger any of the FS3 Critical Capability Levels.

provenance.context: Extracted from the FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2026 citation

blocks.claim: Gemini 2.5 Pro was evaluated against CBRN CCLs.
blocks.excerpt: Gemini 2.5 Pro was evaluated against the CBRN CCLs defined in the FS3 framework. The model does not present novel CBRN uplift risk.

provenance.context: Extracted from the FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2026 citation

blocks.claim: Gemini 2.5 Pro was evaluated against cyber CCLs.
blocks.excerpt: Gemini 2.5 Pro was evaluated against the cyber CCLs defined in the FS3 framework. The model does not present novel cyber uplift risk.
